name: MCP1416T-E_OT
title: MCP1415/MCP1416 (and R pinout variants): 1.5 A single-channel low-side MOSFET driver, 4.5 V to 18 V, SOT-23-5
summary: A single-channel gate driver for a power MOSFET or IGBT referred to ground, in a five-lead SOT-23. One logic input, TTL and CMOS compatible from 3 V to 18 V and tolerant of 5 V below ground, drives a push-pull CMOS stage that sources and sinks 1.5 A peak from a 4.5 V to 18 V supply. The MCP1415 inverts and the MCP1416 does not; the R versions swap the VDD, GND and OUT pins. Into 1000 pF the edges take about 18 ns and 21 ns and the delays 44 ns to 54 ns at 18 V.

circuits.title: Inverting driver switching-time test (MCP1415)
circuits.description: Switching-time measurement for the MCP1415. The driver runs from 18 V with 1 µF plus 0.1 µF (ceramic) from VDD to ground, and its output drives a 1000 pF capacitor to ground. A 0 V to 5 V square wave at 100 Hz with edges of 10 ns or less goes into IN; the output follows inverted, and tD1, tD2, tR and tF are read between the 10 % and 90 % points of the two edges.

equations.name: Operating power dissipation
equations.note: Comes from both output transistors conducting briefly at each transition.

operation.text: One input controls one output. The MCP1415 and MCP1415R invert; the MCP1416 and MCP1416R do not. The input accepts TTL levels or CMOS logic from 3 V to 18 V. Uses named for it include switching power supplies, line driving, driving pulse transformers, solenoids and motors, and logic level translation.
The input is high impedance and TTL/CMOS compatible, with hysteresis between its two thresholds for noise immunity and clean switching from slowly changing signals.

The input sees an effective capacitance of 25 pF and is clamped to GND by a 4.7 V zener, with a diode to VDD. It drives a Schmitt-trigger gate with 300 mV of hysteresis, biased by a 650 µA current source, followed by the inverting (MCP1415) or non-inverting (MCP1416) path and a buffer driving the complementary output MOSFETs. An unused input is to be grounded.
The logic input withstands swings to 5 V below ground.

A CMOS push-pull stage sources and sinks 1.5 A peak at VDD = 18 V. Its low impedance in both output states keeps the driven MOSFET in the commanded state through large transients. Up to 500 mA forced back into the output causes neither damage nor a logic upset. Shoot-through current in the output stage is low, and rise and fall times are matched.

The part resists latch-up anywhere inside its power and voltage ratings. Noise spikes of up to 5 V of either polarity on the ground pin do not damage it. Every pin is protected against ESD to 2.0 kV (human body model) and 300 V (machine model).

Charging gate capacitance quickly takes large current: about 720 mA brings 1000 pF to 18 V in 25 ns. For low supply impedance across a wide frequency range, the part needs two capacitors in parallel from pin 2 (VDD) to pin 4 (GND): 1.0 µF of low-ESR film plus 0.1 µF of ceramic. Both sit next to the driver so the current comes from them and not from the board.
Peak load-discharge current leaves the part by the GND pin, so GND connects to the bias supply return by a low-impedance path.

tD1 is measured from the input passing 10 % on its rising edge, and tD2 from the input passing 90 % on its falling edge, each to the start of the output edge that follows. tR and tF are the output's 10 % to 90 % transition times. The test input is a 0 V to 5 V, 100 Hz square wave with edges of 10 ns or less, at VDD = 18 V into 1000 pF.

Driver dissipation is the sum of three parts: the load's charge and discharge, the quiescent draw (0.65 mA typ with the input high, 0.1 mA typ with it low), and cross-conduction during each output transition, when both output transistors are on for a moment.

Bad component placement leads to false switching, heavy ringing or latch-up. Small trace loop area and inductance come from placing the driver right at the load and the bypass capacitor right at the driver. A ground plane or return trace directly under the output trace lowers its inductance; a plane also screens radiated noise and draws some heat from the part. The recommended layout puts the bypass capacitor across the VDD and GND pins on one side of the driver and the MOSFET (Q1) at its output on the other.
